title: Tech Note: File Names and Pathnames
author: ACI US Technical Support

historical_commentary.text: This note provides two generic, platform-independent utility routines (Path to name, Path only path) for extracting a document's short name and its containing pathname from a long file name, accounting for the differing file-naming rules and path separators of classic Mac OS (colon-separated, 31-char names) versus DOS/Windows (backslash-separated, then-8.3 or up to 255 chars). The specific file-naming limits and path-separator handling described are obsolete relative to modern macOS/Windows file systems, though the general principle of writing platform-abstraction utility code for cross-platform 4D applications remains conceptually relevant.
related_updates: Classic Mac OS's 31-character file name limit and colon-based pathname format were retired along with classic Mac OS itself (Mac OS X onward uses much longer names and POSIX/HFS+ paths)
DOS's 8.3 file name limit is long obsolete; modern Windows (and 4D) support long file names uniformly
4D's current cross-platform document/path-handling commands and the Document/Path length limits have been substantially updated since this 1996 note
